title: Bocksteins Steenrod Squares and Cohomology Operations

items.title: Stable natural cohomology operation
items.statement: For coefficient groups A,B, a degree-r operation is a natural transformation Phi_n: reduced H^n(-;A) -> reduced H^{n+r}(-;B) on based CW complexes. It is stable when it commutes with reduced suspension. Additivity is not assumed.
items.strategy: State the naturality and suspension squares with their directions; reduced cohomology avoids the unreduced degree-zero anomaly.

references.title: May, A Concise Course in Algebraic Topology

items.title: Bockstein connecting operation
items.statement: Assume AC. A short exact coefficient sequence 0->A->B->C->0 induces beta:H^n(X;C)->H^{n+1}(X;A): lift a C-cocycle to B, take its coboundary, and invert A->B. Distinguish the integral sequence 0->Z --m--> Z->Z/m and the mod-m sequence 0->Z/m --m--> Z/m^2->Z/m.
items.strategy: Freeness makes each coefficient cochain map onto. AC is spent only to choose lifts for all simplex values in the general sequence; canonical residue lifts are choice-free.

references.title: Hatcher, Algebraic Topology

items.title: The Bockstein is independent of lift and representative
items.statement: The class beta[c] is independent of the chosen B-cochain lift and of the cocycle representing [c].
items.strategy: Subtract two lifts and use exactness; if the cocycle changes by delta u, lift u and subtract its coboundary before the same comparison.

references.title: Hatcher, Algebraic Topology

items.title: Bocksteins are natural and stable
items.statement: The Bockstein is natural in maps of spaces and morphisms of coefficient sequences, and its reduced version commutes with cohomology suspension.
items.strategy: Use the lift-and-divide definition for naturality in maps and coefficient sequences. Define the signed reduced suspension after proving the CW cone-base quotient comparison by a saturated radial collar, cohomology pair sequences, arbitrary-coefficient homotopy invariance and choice-free excision. The two cohomology connectors anticommute; the degree sign cancels that anticommutation.

references.title: May, A Concise Course in Algebraic Topology

items.title: The mod-two Bockstein is a derivation
items.statement: For beta from 0->Z/m->Z/m^2->Z/m, beta(x cup y)=beta(x) cup y+(-1)^|x|x cup beta(y); over F_2 the sign disappears.
items.strategy: Use canonical residue lifts, expand the coboundary of their cup product by Leibniz, divide by m, and reduce mod m.

references.title: Hatcher, Algebraic Topology

items.title: Natural higher diagonal approximations
items.statement: Over F_2 there are natural degree-i maps D_i:C_*(X)->(C_*(X) tensor C_*(X))_{*+i}, with D_0 Alexander–Whitney and dD_i+D_i d=(1+T)D_{i-1}. They preserve subspaces and are coherently unique.
items.strategy: Induct on i and simplex dimension using the explicit cone contraction of each standard simplex product; fill the carried cycle, then repeat one degree higher for coherent uniqueness.

references.title: Mosher and Tangora, Cohomology Operations and Applications
references.locator: Chapter 2, Acyclic Carrier Theorem and cup-i construction, printed pp.14–16

items.title: Higher cup-i products
items.statement: For mod-two cochains a in C^p and b in C^q, define a cup_i b in C^{p+q-i} by evaluating a tensor b on D_i; cup_i=0 for i<0. The construction restricts to relative cochains.
items.strategy: Define evaluation and verify cup_0 is the published cup product since D_0 is Alexander–Whitney.

references.title: Mosher and Tangora, Cohomology Operations and Applications

items.title: Cup-i coboundary identity
items.statement: Over F_2, delta(a cup_i b)=delta a cup_i b+a cup_i delta b+a cup_{i-1}b+b cup_{i-1}a, with cup_{-1}=0.
items.strategy: Evaluate dD_i+D_i d=(1+T)D_{i-1} against a tensor b and expand the tensor coboundary.

references.title: Mosher and Tangora, Cohomology Operations and Applications
references.locator: Chapter 2, cup-i coboundary formula, printed p.16

items.title: Steenrod squares from cup-i
items.statement: For x in H^n(X;F_2), represented by a, define Sq^k(x)=[a cup_{n-k}a] for 0<=k<=n and zero otherwise.
items.strategy: The cup-i identity with equal cocycle inputs proves the cochain is closed; the next theorem proves independence.

references.title: Mosher and Tangora, Cohomology Operations and Applications
references.locator: Chapter 2, definition of the squares and upper-index convention, printed pp.17–18

items.title: Steenrod squares are well-defined and natural
items.statement: Each Sq^k is independent of cocycle representative and coherent D_i choice, additive, and natural for maps and pairs.
items.strategy: Insert a+delta h, apply the cup-i identity, and cancel polarization terms in characteristic two; use naturality and coherent uniqueness of D_i.

references.title: Mosher and Tangora, Cohomology Operations and Applications
references.locator: Chapter 2, construction, naturality, and relative squares, printed pp.17–19

items.title: Steenrod normalization, instability, suspension, and top square
items.statement: Sq^0=id, Sq^k(x)=0 for k>|x|, Sq^{|x|}(x)=x cup x, and reduced squares commute with suspension.
items.strategy: Normalize the top diagonal for Sq^0 and use cup-i endpoints for instability and top square. Define the reduced cone locally, prove the CW cone-base quotient comparison by a collar, pair sequences and choice-free cohomological excision, then use the relative cup-i connector calculation for suspension.

references.title: Mosher and Tangora, Cohomology Operations and Applications
references.locator: Chapter 2, relative squares and suspension, printed pp.18–20; Chapter 3, Sq^0 proof, printed pp.23–24

references.title: Medina-Mardones, New formulas for cup-i products and fast computation of Steenrod squares
references.locator: Definition 7, Examples 8–9, and Theorem 10, printed pp.8–9

items.title: Cartan coherence for higher diagonals
items.statement: The higher diagonals before and after Alexander–Whitney are coherently chain homotopic, with degree-i boundary equal to the convolution over r+s=i; the homotopies preserve relative subcomplexes.
items.strategy: Put both composites in the tensor-fourfold diagonal carrier and induct on i and simplex dimension; fill the residual carried cycle by the standard-simplex contraction.

references.title: Mosher and Tangora, Cohomology Operations and Applications
references.locator: Chapter 3, external-product Cartan comparison, printed pp.24–25

items.title: Cartan formula for Steenrod squares
items.statement: Sq^k(x cup y)=sum_{i+j=k}Sq^i(x) cup Sq^j(y).
items.strategy: Evaluate Cartan coherence on cocycle representatives; its boundary vanishes in cohomology and the convolution terms give the formula.

references.title: Mosher and Tangora, Cohomology Operations and Applications
Medina-Mardones, New formulas for cup-i products and fast computation of Steenrod squares
references.locator: Definition 7, Examples 8–9, and Theorem 10, printed pp.8–9

items.title: Free cyclic resolution, group cohomology, and cochain transfer
items.statement: For every prime p and C_p=<T>, the augmented free F_p[C_p]-resolution W with one orbit generator e_j in each degree and differentials d e_{2r+1}=(T−1)e_{2r}, d e_{2r}=N e_{2r−1}, N=1+T+...+T^{p−1}, is exact. The equivariant-cochain cohomology H^*(Hom_{F_p[C_p]}(W,F_p)) is F_2[t] with |t|=1 for p=2 and F_p[u]⊗Λ(v) with |u|=2, |v|=1 for odd p. On quotient cellular chains the standard diagonal is Dbar(e_{2r})=sum_{a=0}^r e_{2a}⊗e_{2r−2a}+p(p−1)/2 sum_{a=0}^{r−1}e_{2a+1}⊗e_{2r−2a−1} and Dbar(e_{2r+1})=sum_{a=0}^{2r+1}e_a⊗e_{2r+1−a}; at p=2 every split has coefficient one. For a subgroup H of a finite group G, equivariant cochain transfer is a chain map and transfer after restriction multiplies by [G:H]; in characteristic p this composite vanishes when the index is divisible by p.
items.strategy: Use Steenrod–Epstein V §§5,7. Write F_p[C_p]=F_p[s]/(s^p) with s=T−1 and N=s^{p−1}; the kernels and images of multiplication by s and s^{p−1} prove exactness, including the augmentation. Taking equivariant Hom into the trivial module leaves one zero-differential basis cochain w_j in every degree. Evaluate the explicit quotient diagonal of V Lemma 5.1: its odd-odd coefficient is p(p−1)/2, so p=2 gives powers of w_1 while odd p gives w_1²=0 and the even generator gives all remaining basis elements. With the present positive connecting convention, the canonical mod-p coefficient lift gives beta(w_1)=w_2. For transfer, associate to each left coset gH the representative-independent map c↦g u(g^{-1}c), and sum over the finite quotient G/H. This avoids choosing a transversal; equivariance and the chain-map identity are direct, and transfer after restriction is [G:H].

references.title: N. E. Steenrod and D. B. A. Epstein, Cohomology Operations
references.locator: Chapter V §5, printed pp.67–68, and §7, printed pp.71–72

items.title: Equivariant p-fold external power and diagonal decomposition
items.statement: Assume AC for the equivariant carrier comparisons. For a finite regular cell complex K, with H^*(K;F_p) computed on its cellular cochain model, and u in H^q(K;F_p), the C_p-equivariant external pth-power class P(u) in degree pq on W×K^p is independent of its cocycle and free-resolution choices, natural in K, and restricts on one fiber K^p to u×...×u. Pullback along the diagonal K→K^p has a unique expansion sum_j w_j×D_j(u), with D_j(u) in H^{pq−j}(K;F_p); the coefficient operations D_j are additive. For any carried equivariant diagonal Phi_C:W tensor C(K)→C(K)^{tensor p}, D_j(u) is represented by z↦c^{tensor p}Phi_C(e_j tensor z). More generally, an augmentation-preserving equivariant chain map from a free cellular Gamma-complex, already fixed on a Gamma-subcomplex, extends through any equivariant augmented-acyclic carrier, and two carried extensions agreeing on that subcomplex are equivariantly chain-homotopic relative to it. AC is used exactly to choose orbit representatives and permitted fillings. This finite-cell lemma does not yet assert the later singular-space extension.
items.strategy: Follow Steenrod–Epstein V §§2–3 and VII §§2–4 on the finite regular cellular model. The p-fold tensor of a cellular cocycle is cyclically equivariant because the Koszul sign is trivial for an odd-prime cycle and in characteristic two. Use the source's equivariant interval construction for representative independence and its free-acyclic comparison for resolution independence, explicitly declaring AC for the recursive orbit-filling choices. On the diagonal with trivial K-action, identify equivariant cochains degreewise as the finite direct sum of w_j tensor cellular cochains, so no Künneth splitting choice is needed. For additivity, partition the finitely many mixed binary words into free cyclic orbits and use the transfer. Prove diagonal pullback kills each transferred class by the onto restriction supplied by the explicit contraction of the underlying standard W and transfer after restriction equals p=0. Do not claim transfer itself vanishes. The later cyclic-power lemma, not this finite-cell helper, owns the arbitrary singular-space extension.

references.title: N. E. Steenrod and D. B. A. Epstein, Cohomology Operations
references.locator: Chapter V §§2–3, printed pp.60–64; Chapter VII §2, printed pp.99–101, §3, printed pp.103–104, and §4, printed pp.104–105

items.title: Wreath double-power comparison and coefficient transposition
items.statement: Assume AC as in the finite cellular p-fold-power construction. For a finite regular cell complex, the iterated power through W_1×W_2^p and the one-step p²-power through the row–column C_p×C_p action have the same double-diagonal pullback. If D_{j,k}(x) is the coefficient of w_j×w_k in that class for x in cellular H^q(K;F_p), then D_{j,k}(x)=(-1)^{jk+p(p−1)q/2}D_{k,j}(x). This comparison does not yet assert an Adem relation or the singular-space extension.
items.strategy: Follow Steenrod–Epstein VIII §1 through Lemma 1.3. Let alpha translate rows and beta translate columns of the p×p coordinate array. The product W_1×W_2^p is free acyclic for alpha×beta. On a pure tensor, the direct p²-power and the iterated p-fold power are the same epsilon factors times the same p² copies of a cocycle after signed regrouping. Truncate W_2 at the prescribed skeleton above p²q+1 before applying the finite construction; finite-degree cellular cochains stabilize. Pull back along W_2→W_2^p and the double diagonal of K, and decompose uniquely in the w_j×w_k basis. The transpose lambda(i,j)=(j,i) conjugates alpha and beta. The tensor symmetry on resolution degrees contributes (-1)^{jk}; lambda is a product of p(p−1)/2 transpositions, so the degree-q coefficient line contributes (-1)^{p(p−1)q/2}. Invariance of the direct tensor class and uniqueness of coefficients give the stated symmetry. No Cartan formula or Adem coefficient extraction is used here; those remain later items.

references.title: N. E. Steenrod and D. B. A. Epstein, Cohomology Operations
references.locator: Chapter VIII §1, opening through Lemma 1.3, printed pp.115–118

items.title: Finite-cellular cyclic squares, Cartan formula, and cyclic-basis action
items.statement: Assume AC. For the mod-two coefficients D_j of the finite cellular cyclic power of a degree-q class x, define Sq_cyc^i(x)=D_{q−i}(x) for 0≤i≤q and zero outside that range. These operations are additive and natural, satisfy Sq_cyc^0=id, instability, the top-square identity, and the external and internal Cartan formulas. On H^*(BC_2;F_2)=F_2[t], computed through finite skeleta, Sq_cyc^j(t^r)=binom(r,j)t^{r+j}. This item does not identify Sq_cyc with the singular cup-i squares.
items.strategy: Specialize the cyclic power to p=2. Compare the power of an external product with the product of powers through the explicit diagonal on the standard cyclic resolution; coefficient uniqueness gives D_k(x×y)=sum_{a+b=k}D_a(x)×D_b(y), hence Cartan after reversing indices. The zero resolution coordinate is the diagonal pullback of x×x. For the Sq_cyc^0 coefficient, use the finite q-skeleton and a cocycle-defined map to S^q to reduce to a scalar; compute the scalar in degree one on the two-edge circle and propagate it by external Cartan. For the basis calculation, replace the nonregular one-cell projective skeleton by Q_N=(sd L_N)/(±1), where L_N is the cross-polytope boundary; prove directly that Q_N is a finite regular simplicial complex realizing RP^N. Compare its cellular diagonal with the singular Alexander--Whitney diagonal through the relative carrier theorem, identify the restricted group-resolution basis t^d=[w_d], and only then apply Cartan and the binomial theorem on Q_N. Propagate AC from carrier comparison and field duality, and do not claim the later singular cup-i identification.

references.title: N. E. Steenrod and D. B. A. Epstein, Cohomology Operations
references.locator: Chapter VII Lemmas 4.4 and 4.7, printed pages 105--108; section 5 and Theorem 6.7, printed pages 108--114

items.title: Adem double-power comparison
items.statement: For the finite-cellular mod-two cyclic squares, the row–column comparison gives an explicit symmetric double-coefficient identity. If a,b are positive integers with 0<a<2b, s satisfies 2^s>a, q=2^s−1+b, and x has degree q, the identity reduces to Sq_cyc^a Sq_cyc^b(x)=sum_{r=0}^{floor(a/2)} binom(b−r−1,a−2r) Sq_cyc^{a+b−r} Sq_cyc^r(x). This is the high-degree numerical calculation; descent to all degrees and comparison with singular cup-i squares remain for the following theorem.
items.strategy: Set p=2 in the wreath coefficient symmetry, so both signs disappear. Choose one explicit finite regular projective model Q_N large enough for every cyclic-basis degree in the finite extraction, then expand the iterated total cyclic square using Cartan and Sq_cyc^j(w_r)=binom(r,j)w_{r+j}. Comparing the w_{2q−a}×w_{2q−ell} coordinate with its transpose gives the two explicit sums in Steenrod--Epstein VIII Theorem 1.5. Put ell=q+b and q=2^s−1+b. The first binomial vanishes unless its inner index is b; complement the second lower index to a−2r. For 0<a<2b, nonzero terms have r<b, and the binary Lucas calculation reduces binom(2^s−1+b−r,a−2r) to binom(b−r−1,a−2r) when 2^s>a. Record the finite range r≤floor(a/2). Do not invoke the final Adem theorem or its later descent and singular-comparison steps.

references.title: Steenrod and Epstein, Cohomology Operations
references.locator: Chapter VIII Convention 1.4 and Theorem 1.5 through its high-degree calculation, printed pages 118--119

items.title: Finite-cellular cyclic squares agree with singular cup-i squares
items.statement: Assume AC. For every finite oriented regular cell complex K, a cell-carried cellular-to-singular chain comparison induces an isomorphism iota^*:H_sing^*(K;F_2)→H_cell^*(K;F_2), and iota^*Sq^i(y)=Sq_cyc^i(iota^*y) for every degree and integer i. The equality is independent of the carried comparison and higher-diagonal choices. No arbitrary-space extension is asserted.
items.strategy: Subdivide the finite regular complex and send each cellular generator to its mod-two fundamental subdivision chain. The cellular comparison theorem makes this a homology isomorphism; under AC, splitting the acyclic mapping cone shows that its dual is a cohomology isomorphism. Package the singular higher diagonals and the cellular cyclic diagonal as equivariant maps out of W tensor C_cell(K). After the cellular-to-singular comparison, both maps lie in the same closed-cell diagonal carrier, whose tensor singular chains are augmented acyclic by contractibility and Eilenberg--Zilber. Equivariant carrier uniqueness gives a homotopy. Evaluating its e_{q-i} coordinate on a singular cocycle identifies the cup-i square with Sq_cyc^i, including unnormalized degeneracies and both index endpoints.

references.title: N. E. Steenrod and D. B. A. Epstein, Cohomology Operations
references.locator: Chapter V section 2, printed pages 60--61, and Chapter VIII section 2, printed pages 123--124

references.title: Mosher and Tangora, Cohomology Operations and Applications
references.locator: Chapter 2, Acyclic Carrier Theorem and construction and independence of cup-i squares, printed pages 14--18

items.title: Natural singular-cohomology identities are detected on finite regular complexes
items.statement: Assume AC. Fix a prime p, m,n≥0, and a natural family R_X:H^m(X;F_p)→H^n(X;F_p). If R_K=0 for every finite regular cell complex K, then R_X=0 for every space X. Additivity and a simultaneous finite model are not required.
items.strategy: For a finite mod-p singular cycle, form the finite Delta complex generated by its supporting simplices and all face restrictions, identifying face occurrences with the same singular-simplex label and retaining the actual coefficients; the cycle equation makes the resulting weighted top chain a cycle. Its second barycentric subdivision is a finite regular simplicial complex, and the explicit subdivision chain homotopy preserves the represented homology class. Naturality and the Kronecker pairing reduce vanishing on an arbitrary space to the finite hypothesis. Finally prove evaluation injective over F_p directly: if a cocycle vanishes on cycles, define a functional on boundaries using preimages and, under AC, extend it across a vector-space complement to obtain a cobounding cochain.

references.title: Allen Hatcher, Algebraic Topology
references.locator: Section 2.1, finite Delta-complex realization of cycles on printed pages 108--109, subdivision chain homotopy on printed pages 121--123, and Exercise 23 on printed page 133

references.title: N. E. Steenrod and D. B. A. Epstein, Cohomology Operations
references.locator: Chapter VIII section 2, extension to arbitrary singular cohomology, printed pages 123--124

items.title: Adem relations for Steenrod squares
items.statement: Assume AC. For positive integers 0<a<2b and every singular mod-two cohomology class, Sq^aSq^b=sum_{j=0}^{floor(a/2)} binom(b-j-1,a-2j)Sq^{a+b-j}Sq^j, with binomial coefficients reduced mod two and all out-of-range operations and coefficients zero.
items.strategy: Transfer the finite-cellular high-degree coefficient identity to singular cup-i squares through the proved carried comparison. Compute the boundary-of-a-triangle model of S^1, use external Cartan and instability to show every square composition P satisfies P(u times v)=P(u) times v for its degree-one generator, and use the cohomological Kunneth isomorphism to make cross product with v injective. Descend from the unbounded degrees 2^s-1+b to every degree on finite regular complexes. The proved finite-cycle detection lemma then extends the natural residual operation to every space. Propagate AC exactly from the cyclic/carrier comparison, finite-cycle detection, and additive Kunneth bijectivity.

references.title: Steenrod and Epstein, Cohomology Operations
references.locator: Chapter VII Lemma 6.8, printed page 114, and Chapter VIII Convention 1.4 and Theorem 1.5, printed pages 118–119

items.title: Bockstein parity recurrence for Steenrod squares
items.statement: For the mod-two Bockstein and 0<=j<=p on H^p(-;F_2), beta Sq^j is zero for odd j and equals Sq^{j+1} for even j. The cochain proof is choice-free.
items.strategy: Construct the signed integral cup-i system in the standard simplex carrier and reduce it modulo two. For an integral residue lift c of a mod-two cocycle with delta c=2h, divide the signed coboundary of c cup_i c by two. The two h terms are a mod-two coboundary, while the two c cup_{i-1} c terms cancel for odd j and add to Sq^{j+1} for even j.

references.title: Mosher and Tangora, Cohomology Operations and Applications in Homotopy Theory
references.locator: Chapter 2 signed cup-i coboundary calculation, printed pages 15--16, and Chapter 3 Lemma 1, printed page 23

items.title: Sq^1 is the mod-two Bockstein
items.statement: For every space and every nonnegative degree, Sq^1 equals the Bockstein of 0->F_2->Z/4->F_2. The equality and its cyclic residue-lift proof require no AC.
items.strategy: Apply the proved Bockstein parity recurrence at j=0 and use the independently proved normalization Sq^0=id. Retain the cyclic residue-lift convention and its choice-free status.

references.title: Steenrod and Epstein, Cohomology Operations
Mosher and Tangora, Cohomology Operations and Applications in Homotopy Theory
references.locator: Chapter 3 Lemma 1 and its j=0 consequence, printed page 23

items.title: Total Steenrod square
items.statement: On the ordinary graded direct sum H^*(X;F_2), define Sq(x)=sum_{i>=0}Sq^i(x), with the sum finite on every element by instability and finite degree support. It is a natural unital ring endomorphism of the underlying total cohomology ring, not a degree-preserving map and not a map into a completion.
items.strategy: Define the total operation first on a homogeneous class and then on the finite-support graded direct sum. Instability proves elementwise finiteness; additivity and naturality descend termwise. Summing the Cartan formula over the finitely many indices proves multiplicativity, and Sq^0=id plus instability proves unit preservation.

references.title: Hatcher, Algebraic Topology
Mosher and Tangora, Cohomology Operations and Applications in Homotopy Theory
references.locator: Chapter 3, definition and ring-homomorphism proof for the total square, printed page 25

items.title: Wu classes of a closed manifold
items.statement: Assume AC. For a possibly empty or disconnected closed n-manifold M with its canonical mod-two fundamental class, v_k is the unique class in H^k(M;F_2) satisfying <v_k cup x,[M]_2>=<Sq^k x,[M]_2> for every x in H^{n-k}, for 0<=k<=n; put v_k=0 outside this range and v=sum_{k=0}^n v_k. Then v_0=1 and v_k=0 when 2k>n.
items.strategy: Use additivity of Sq^k and the canonical mod-two fundamental class to define the linear functional x↦<Sq^kx,[M]_2>. Assuming AC exactly as required by the published perfect-pairing supplier, invert the first adjoint of the cup pairing to obtain its unique representative v_k. Normalization gives v_0=1, while instability gives v_k=0 for 2k>n.

references.title: Husemöller, Joachim, Jurčo, and Schottenloher, Basic Bundle Theory and K-Cohomology Invariants
references.locator: Chapter 11, Definition 5.2 and its displayed pairing calculation, printed page 132

items.title: Cyclic p-fold power construction
items.statement: Assume AC. For prime p, the free cyclic resolution and equivariant p-fold external power define natural additive singular operations D_j:H^q(X;F_p)->H^{pq-j}(X;F_p), zero for j<0 or j>(p-1)q, with D_0(x)=x^p. They agree with the finite cellular coefficients. For odd p their normalizer congruences, positive-Bockstein identities beta D_{2r}=-D_{2r-1} and beta D_{2r-1}=0, external product formula, and top value D_{(p-1)q}(x)=(-1)^{m q(q+1)/2}(m!)^q x, m=(p-1)/2, give the exact normalization data; for p=2 the top scalar is one.
items.strategy: Construct a strictly natural equivariant p-fold singular diagonal on universal simplices using the relative carrier theorem and define D_j by evaluating its e_j-coordinate. Prove representative and carrier independence, kill mixed tensor words by transfer to obtain additivity, and identify D_0 with cup pth power. Compare this construction to the finite cellular one inside the closed-cell carrier. On finite complexes prove the sharp range by the q-skeleton and sphere map, compute the normalizer congruences from the Vandermonde sign and H^*(BC_p), derive the external formula from the cyclic diagonal, and track the library's positive Bockstein sign. Compute a_1 from the actual two-edge-circle carrier formula and propagate it by the external formula. Use the mod-p finite-detection supplier only for the one-input range, congruence, and top identities on arbitrary spaces.

references.title: Steenrod and Epstein, Cohomology Operations
references.locator: Chapter VII §§2–5, printed pp.99–112, and Chapter VIII §2, printed pp.122–124

items.title: Mod-p reduced power operations
items.statement: Assume AC. For an odd prime p, a class x of degree q, and m=(p−1)/2, define P^i x=(-1)^{i+m(q²+q)/2}(m!)^(−q) D_{(q−2i)(p−1)}x in H^{q+2i(p−1)}(X;F_p), with D_j=0 for j<0; define beta P^i by composing with the mod-p Bockstein. Negative i are zero, P^0 is the identity by the top-power normalization, and P^i x=0 for 2i>q.
items.strategy: Use the singular cyclic coefficient operations supplied by the previous lemma and propagate its AC assumption. This is Steenrod–Epstein VII Definition 6.1 with m=(p−1)/2 and sign exponent i+m(q²+q)/2, but with the factorial factor corrected to (m!)^(−q): the printed positive exponent conflicts with VII Lemma 6.4, and p=5,q=1 would otherwise give P^0=-id. Degree follows from pq−(q−2i)(p−1)=q+2i(p−1), while the top-index identity gives P^0=id and a negative cyclic index gives instability. Define beta P^i as the well-defined positive mod-p Bockstein composite and set negative i operations to zero.

references.title: Steenrod and Epstein, Cohomology Operations
references.locator: Chapter VII Definition 6.1 and Lemmas 6.3–6.4, printed pp.112–113

items.title: Reduced powers satisfy naturality, instability, Cartan, and Adem relations
items.statement: Assume AC. For odd p, the normalized P^i and beta P^i are natural stable additive operations, P^0=id, P^i x=0 when 2i>deg x, and P^{deg x/2}x=x^p when deg x is even. They satisfy Cartan P^k(xy)=sum_{i+j=k}P^i(x)P^j(y). For nonnegative a,b with a<pb, P^aP^b=sum_{t=0}^{floor(a/p)}(-1)^{a+t}binom((p−1)(b−t)−1,a−pt)P^{a+b−t}P^t. For nonnegative a,b with a<=pb, P^a beta P^b=sum_{t=0}^{floor(a/p)}(-1)^{a+t}binom((p−1)(b−t),a−pt) beta P^{a+b−t}P^t + sum_{t=0}^{floor((a−1)/p)}(-1)^{a+t−1}binom((p−1)(b−t)−1,a−pt−1)P^{a+b−t} beta P^t, with out-of-range binomials zero and sums with upper bound below zero empty.
items.strategy: Normalize the cyclic coefficients to prove naturality, additivity, P^0, instability, top power and Cartan, including Wilson's finite product identity and full sign cancellation. Compute P^j and beta P^j on H^*(C_p;F_p) from Cartan, top power and the positive Bockstein. Expand the normalized double cyclic power into its four parity rows and apply the wreath symmetry. For the first relation choose high degree q=2(1+...+p^{s−1})+2b; for the beta relation choose q=2p^s+2b. Exact coefficient selection and the base-p binomial calculation give the two displayed sums. Descend finite-complex identities degree by degree with the circle generator and Kunneth injectivity, then use the mod-p finite detector for arbitrary spaces. Prove stability separately from external Cartan and a locally defined reduced cone, a choice-free cohomological quotient comparison, and the signed cone-pair suspension model. Propagate AC from the cyclic/wreath, detector, and additive Kunneth suppliers.

references.title: Steenrod and Epstein, Cohomology Operations
references.locator: Chapter VII §§4–6 and Chapter VIII §§1–2, printed pp.104–124

items.title: Mod-two cohomology ring of infinite real projective space
items.statement: Assume AC. Infinite real projective space has H^*(RP^infinity;F_2)=F_2[a] with |a|=1. For every integer n>=0, restriction along RP^n->RP^infinity is an isomorphism in degrees at most n and sends a to the finite generator when n>=1, and to zero when n=0.
items.strategy: The standard filtration makes RP^infinity a CW complex with one cell in every nonnegative degree. The integral incidence numbers 0 and 2 reduce to zero over F_2, so cellular homology and hence singular homology is F_2 in every degree; skeletal inclusions induce the identity in every cellular degree they contain. Natural field duality gives the same cohomology groups and restriction isomorphisms. For finite RP^n, use complementary coordinate projective subspaces meeting at one point. Pair exact sequences, explicit complement retractions, excision and the local coordinate relative-cup generator show that the product of the unique positive-degree classes in complementary degrees is the top class. Induct to obtain every power of the degree-one class without a B-page dependency. Detect each infinite power on a finite skeleton. Propagate AC from field duality and the local relative-product supplier.

references.title: Hatcher, Algebraic Topology
references.locator: Theorem 3.19 and its complete proof, printed pp.220–221

items.title: Mod-two cohomology rings of complex projective spaces
items.statement: Assume AC. For every integer n>=0, H^*(CP^n;F_2)=F_2[c_n]/(c_n^{n+1}), |c_n|=2, where c_n is reduction mod two of the normalized integral generator, and H^*(CP^infinity;F_2)=F_2[c], |c|=2. Standard skeletal restrictions preserve the generators and are isomorphisms through the dimension of the finite skeleton; all odd cohomology groups vanish.
items.strategy: Construct the compatible CW filtration directly by attaching a real 2r-disk to CP^(r-1), with the cell oriented by its ordered complex coordinates. No adjacent cell dimensions occur, so cellular comparison gives integral homology and natural skeletal generators. UCT gives the integral and mod-two additive cohomology groups; reduction of the normalized integral degree-two evaluator is the unique mod-two degree-two class. For finite CP^n, complementary coordinate CP^i and CP^j meet at one point. Pair exact sequences, explicit complement retractions, excision and the local coordinate relative-cup generator show that the unique complementary-degree classes have nonzero top product. Induct to obtain the finite truncated rings without citing either published B-page projective example, then detect every infinite power on a finite skeleton. Propagate AC exactly from UCT and the local relative-product supplier.

references.title: Hatcher, Algebraic Topology
references.locator: Theorem 3.19 and its complete proof, printed pp.220–221

title: Bocksteins Steenrod Squares and Cohomology Operations — Examples

items.title: Bockstein detects integral two-torsion in real projective space
items.statement: Assume AC. For the unique nonzero class a in H^1(RP^n;F_2), where n>=2 is an integer, beta_Z(a) generates H^2(RP^n;Z)=Z/2 and the mod-two Bockstein satisfies beta_2(a)=Sq^1(a)=a^2.
items.strategy: Use the A-level projective cellular boundary calculation and UCT to derive H^1(RP^n;Z)=0 and H^2(RP^n;Z)=Z/2 explicitly for n>=2, including Ext(Z/2,Z)=Z/2 from its two-term free resolution. For the canonical zero-one integral lift c-hat of a mod-two singular cocycle c, write delta(c-hat)=2h. If [h] vanished, subtracting twice an integral primitive would give an integral degree-one cocycle lifting c; the calculated H^1=0 would make a a mod-two coboundary. Thus beta_Z(a) is the nonzero generator. Separately beta_2=Sq^1 and the top-square formula give beta_2(a)=a^2, which the A-level projective ring supplier makes nonzero. Propagate AC exactly from UCT and that ring supplier.

references.title: Hatcher, Algebraic Topology

items.title: Steenrod squares on real projective space
items.statement: Assume AC. Let H^*(RP^infinity;F_2)=F_2[a] with |a|=1. For all integers i,j>=0, Sq^i(a^j)=binom(j,i)a^{j+i}, with the binomial coefficient reduced mod two. On RP^n the same formula holds for the finite generator a_n in F_2[a_n]/(a_n^{n+1}); in particular the right side is zero when j+i>n.
items.strategy: Normalization, the top-square identity, and instability give Sq(a)=a+a^2. Sum the finite Cartan formulas to prove total multiplicativity, then expand Sq(a^j)=(a+a^2)^j and compare the homogeneous component of degree j+i. For RP^n, reduce the A-level integral cellular boundary coefficients zero or two modulo two, use cellular comparison and field duality to obtain one cohomology generator in degrees 0 through n and zero above, and use restriction of the infinite powers to identify the truncated polynomial ring. Steenrod and cup-product naturality then give the finite formula, including j+i>n, i=0, j=0, and i>j. Propagate AC exactly from the infinite ring supplier and field duality.

references.title: Hatcher, Algebraic Topology
references.locator: §4.L, formula (*) and its derivation, printed pp.490–491

items.title: Steenrod squares on complex projective space mod two
items.statement: Assume AC. Let H^*(CP^infinity;F_2)=F_2[c] with |c|=2. For all integers i,j>=0, Sq^{2i}(c^j)=binom(j,i)c^{j+i}, with the coefficient reduced mod two, and Sq^r(c^j)=0 for every odd r. The same formulas hold in H^*(CP^n;F_2)=F_2[c_n]/(c_n^{n+1}), so the even formula vanishes when j+i>n.
items.strategy: The mod-two complex-projective-space ring has no odd groups, so normalization, the top square, and instability give Sq(c)=c+c^2. Sum the finite Cartan formulas, expand Sq(c^j)=(c+c^2)^j, and compare degree 2j+r: only even r=2i occur and their coefficients are binom(j,i). Steenrod and cup-product naturality restrict the calculation to CP^n, where the quotient gives the precise truncation. Propagate AC from the ring supplier.

references.title: Hatcher, Algebraic Topology

items.title: The relation Sq^1Sq^1=0
items.statement: For every space X, every integer n>=0, and every x in H^n(X;F_2), Sq^1Sq^1(x)=0. The calculation is choice-free.
items.strategy: For a zero/one integer lift c-hat of a mod-two cocycle, write delta(c-hat)=2h. Reduction modulo four proves beta_2=rho beta_Z. An integral cocycle itself lifts its mod-two reduction, so beta_Z rho=0 directly; hence beta_2 squared is zero. Substitute Sq^1=beta_2. This is choice-free and independent of the general Adem theorem.

references.title: Hatcher, Algebraic Topology

items.title: Wu classes of a closed surface
items.statement: Assume AC. Let M be a nonempty closed connected topological surface. After choosing one generator in every integral orientation stalk, let epsilon be the degree-one mod-two cocycle recording whether orientation transport along a singular one-simplex reverses that generator. Its class w_1(M) is independent of the generator family. Then v_0(M)=1, v_1(M)=w_1(M), and v_i(M)=0 for i>1; moreover v_1(M)=0 exactly when M is orientable.
items.strategy: Use AC once to choose a generator in every orientation stalk. Prove the resulting edge-sign cochain epsilon is a cocycle and changes by a coboundary under a new generator family. For the signed local zero-cochain c, write delta c=2b and identify b mod two with epsilon. Cap c with a finite canonical twisted fundamental cycle C through the pairing O_M tensor O_M -> Z; the exact cap sign gives an integral lift Z of [M]_2 with partial Z=2W and W=-b cap C. Evaluate the mod-four Bockstein Sq^1 on Z, cancel two integrally, and use cap-cup adjunction to prove <Sq^1 x,[M]_2>=<w_1 cup x,[M]_2>. Perfect-pairing uniqueness gives v_1=w_1; normalization and instability give all remaining Wu classes. Finally prove both orientability directions by changing the generator family by a primitive of epsilon and checking local continuity in orientation charts.

references.title: Ranicki, Algebraic and Geometric Surgery
references.locator: Definition 4.1(iii), Remark 4.2, and Proposition 4.3(ii), printed page 49

references.title: Hatcher, correction to the last two paragraphs of Algebraic Topology page 335
references.locator: Complete one-page correction, including the twisted fundamental class and the constant/orientation-coefficient duality statements

references.title: Davis and Kirk, Lecture Notes in Algebraic Topology
references.locator: Chapter 5, Section 2.2, Orientations and Poincare duality, printed pages 100--103

items.title: Top squares do not determine lower squares
items.statement: Assume AC. The suspension of the generator of H^1(RP^2;F_2) and the generator of H^2(S^2;F_2) both square to zero, but their Sq^1 values are nonzero and zero respectively. Thus the top-square formula does not determine all lower squares.
items.strategy: The standard cone-pair cohomology suspension is an isomorphism, so stability carries the nonzero projective Sq^1(a)=a^2 through suspension. Obtain a^2 nonzero by restricting the A-level infinite polynomial generator through degree two. Obtain H^3(RP^2;F_2)=0 by reducing the A-level zero-or-two cellular incidence matrix modulo two, applying cellular comparison and field duality. The A-level sphere-homology corollary plus the same field duality makes the sphere groups in degrees three and four zero. These target-group calculations prove Sq^1(y)=0 and both top squares zero. AC is inherited exactly from the projective Bockstein, the infinite-ring supplier, and field duality.

generation.truth_risk: The suspended projective generator and its first square must remain nonzero, both top squares must vanish, and the reduced suspension convention must match the stability theorem.
generation.counterexample_search: Checked the cone-pair suspension isomorphism, the RP^2 Bockstein and ring calculations, and the mod-two sphere cohomology calculation.

references.title: May, A Concise Course in Algebraic Topology

items.title: Steenrod squares do not all lift integrally
items.statement: Assume AC. There is no integral-valued degree-two cohomology operation whose coefficient reduction is Sq^2 on every space, degree, and class. This does not apply to Sq^1, which has the integral Bockstein as an integral-valued lift.
items.strategy: Use u=a^3 in H^3(RP^infinity;F_2). The projective formula gives Sq^2(u)=binom(3,2)a^5=a^5 nonzero. Build the infinite cellular complex from the compatible A-level finite RP skeleta; its incidence differentials alternate 0 and 2, so H_4=0 and H_5=Z/2. UCT with G=Z then makes H^5(RP^infinity;Z)=0 because both Ext(0,Z) and Hom(Z/2,Z) vanish. Thus no integral value can reduce to a^5, even without naturality. Separately, for a zero/one lift c-hat with delta(c-hat)=2h, compare the integral and mod-four cyclic Bocksteins to prove rho beta_Z=beta_2=Sq^1 as natural operations. Propagate AC exactly from the projective formula, UCT, and general Bockstein naturality supplier.

references.title: Hatcher, Algebraic Topology
Miller, Algebraic Topology notes

title: Local Coefficients, Twisted Homology, and Duality

items.title: Fundamental groupoid of a space
items.statement: Pi_1(X) has points as objects and endpoint-fixed homotopy classes of paths as arrows, composed in first-path-first traversal order; constants are units and reversal gives inverses.
items.strategy: Use published concatenation laws; impose no connectedness or basepoint.

references.title: Davis and Kirk, Lecture Notes in Algebraic Topology

items.title: Vertex groups recover the fundamental group
items.statement: Reversal gives a canonical group isomorphism pi_1(X,x)->Aut_{Pi_1(X)}(x) between the published first-loop-first multiplication and categorical composition. The identity on loop classes is an anti-isomorphism.
items.strategy: Reverse each loop class and use reversal of concatenation to reconcile the two multiplication orders; record explicitly why the identity-on-classes map reverses products.

references.title: Hatcher, Algebraic Topology

items.title: Local systems and pullback
items.statement: A left R-module local system is a functor L:Pi_1(X)->R-Mod whose arrows are isomorphisms. Put f^*L=L∘Pi_1(f); morphisms are natural transformations. Work componentwise.
items.strategy: Spell out fibers and transports; do not smuggle universal covers into arbitrary spaces.

references.title: Davis and Kirk, Lecture Notes in Algebraic Topology

items.title: Local systems correspond to group-ring modules
items.statement: Assume AC. For nonempty connected CW X and basepoint x, evaluation gives an equivalence between left R-module local systems and left R[pi_1(X,x)]-modules. A path family builds a quasi-inverse; the equivalence is canonical only up to natural isomorphism.
items.strategy: Use characteristic-disk images and the weak topology to prove a connected CW complex path connected. Restrict to the vertex group. Conversely use AC exactly once to select paths from x to all points and conjugate transport; compare two choices naturally.

references.title: Davis and Kirk, Lecture Notes in Algebraic Topology

items.title: Right action on universal-cover chains
items.statement: For the published left deck action of pi, set c·g=g^{-1}c on C_*(X-tilde;R), extended R-linearly. The boundary is right R[pi]-linear.
items.strategy: Check (c·g)·h=c·(gh); deck maps commute with boundaries. The inverse is required by the traversal convention.

references.title: Davis and Kirk, Lecture Notes in Algebraic Topology

items.title: Singular and cellular local chain complexes
items.statement: Define intrinsic singular local chains as the direct sum of first-vertex fibers with transport on the zeroth face, and local cochains as the corresponding product with inverse transport. For connected CW X these identify with the universal-cover tensor and equivariant-Hom complexes; define the cellular tensor/Hom complexes similarly. Disconnected universal-cover coordinates require supplied component basepoints, while the intrinsic complexes do not.
items.strategy: Write the intrinsic boundary and coboundary, check the transported zeroth face, balanced relation and typed equivariance phi(c·g)=g^{-1}phi(c), then define cellular tensor/Hom models without pre-asserting their later skeletal-relative identification.

references.title: Hatcher, Algebraic Topology

items.title: Twisted boundaries square to zero and ignore lift bases
items.statement: Both local differentials square to zero. Changing cell lifts conjugates group-ring incidence matrices by diagonal units and gives a chain isomorphism after tensoring.
items.strategy: Use d^2 before tensoring and triple connecting maps cellularly. Rescale changed lift coordinates using the inverse in c·g=g^{-1}c.

references.title: Davis and Kirk, Lecture Notes in Algebraic Topology

items.title: Homology and cohomology with local coefficients
items.statement: Define H_n(X,A;L) and H^n(X,A;L) from relative groupoid chains/cochains, equivalently universal-cover tensor and equivariant-Hom models for connected CW pairs. Constant systems recover ordinary coefficients.
items.strategy: Use quotient chains and kernels of restriction; compare models by transporting the chosen vertex coefficient.

references.title: Hatcher, Algebraic Topology

items.title: Functoriality with coefficient morphisms
items.statement: For f:X->Y, L->f^*K induces f_* in homology, while f^*K->L induces f^* in cohomology. At fixed X both are covariant in coefficient morphisms. Composition and homotopy invariance hold with the specified pullback comparisons.
items.strategy: Compose simplices with f and use the correctly directed fiber map; check differential compatibility by transport naturality and use a transported prism for homotopies.

references.title: Davis and Kirk, Lecture Notes in Algebraic Topology

items.title: Cellular chains compute local homology
items.statement: For a CW pair and local system, cellular local chains compute singular local homology. After lift choices the nth group is a direct sum of fibers over n-cells and its boundary is the group-ring incidence matrix.
items.strategy: Filter by skeleta, use local excision to concentrate relative homology in cell degree, and induct through pair exact sequences.

references.title: Davis and Kirk, Lecture Notes in Algebraic Topology

items.title: Pair exact sequences with local coefficients
items.statement: Every pair with a local system on X has natural long exact homology and cohomology sequences using the restriction to A and the stated variances.
items.strategy: Apply the standard connecting-map construction to the degreewise short exact local chain and cochain sequences.

references.title: Davis and Kirk, Lecture Notes in Algebraic Topology

items.title: Excision and Mayer–Vietoris with local coefficients
items.statement: Local homology and cohomology satisfy excision and natural Mayer–Vietoris sequences for an excisive cover, provided all restrictions come from one ambient local system.
items.strategy: Subdivision transports coefficients within each simplex, so the standard small-chain/prism proof applies. Derive Mayer–Vietoris from the small-chain short exact sequence.

references.title: Hatcher, Algebraic Topology

items.title: Cellular cochains compute cohomology with local coefficients
items.statement: For a CW pair and local system, the cellular cochain complex obtained from the skeletal filtration computes singular cohomology with local coefficients. In the connected universal-cover model it is the equivariant Hom complex on cellular chains, with the published right-chain convention converted to the left action before applying Hom.
items.strategy: Use the skeletal filtration and local excision to identify relative cohomology of successive skeleta with the cellular equivariant-Hom groups. The pair exact sequences and a dimension induction compare cellular and singular cocycles, boundaries, and restriction maps; the handedness equality phi(c·g)=g^{-1}phi(c) makes every differential typed. Use the direct local-coefficient cohomological excision and small-cochain Mayer-Vietoris theorem for skeletal concentration and the telescope.

references.title: Davis and Kirk, Lecture Notes in Algebraic Topology

items.title: Compactly supported cohomology with local coefficients
items.statement: For locally compact Hausdorff X, H_c^k(X;L)=colim_{K compact}H^k(X,X\K;L). Proper maps with correctly directed coefficient morphisms induce pullbacks.
items.strategy: Repeat the published support colimit with local cochains and state the common-larger-support equivalence.

references.title: Hatcher, Algebraic Topology

items.title: The orientation system is a local system
items.statement: The published orientation system O_M defines Pi_1(M)->Ab; O_M^R=O_M tensor_Z R is a rank-one R-local system whose loop monodromy is the orientation character.
items.strategy: Use published path transport, homotopy invariance, and concatenation; tensor stalkwise and identify generator exchange with sign -1.

references.title: Davis and Kirk, Lecture Notes in Algebraic Topology

items.title: Orientation local system on a manifold with boundary
items.statement: For compact M with boundary A and interior N, choose a collar push-in r:M->N and define O_M^R=r^*O_N^R. Different push-ins give specified naturally isomorphic systems, and the collar identifies the restriction to A with O_A^R in the outward-normal-first convention.
items.strategy: Use a collar push-in rather than boundary-point local top homology, compare two push-ins by a supplied homotopy and its path transports, and calculate the outward-normal-first boundary identification in collar charts.

references.title: Hatcher, Algebraic Topology
Davis and Kirk, Lecture Notes in Algebraic Topology

items.title: Canonical twisted fundamental classes over compact subsets
items.statement: For a boundaryless n-manifold, every compact K has a unique compatible class in H_n(M,M\K;O_M^R) whose point-local value is orientation cycle o_x carrying coefficient o_x tensor 1. For compact M with actual boundary A, there is a unique relative class [M,A]^tw with these interior values and outward-normal-first boundary [A]^tw.
items.strategy: Type the canonical point value with both orientation factors, derive closed-support Mayer–Vietoris for local chains, prove existence/uniqueness first for convex and finite chart supports, enlarge arbitrary compact supports away from finite boundary chains, glue finitely many chart pieces, and use collar cores plus the local product-boundary calculation for the compact boundary pair.

references.title: Hatcher, Algebraic Topology
Davis and Kirk, Lecture Notes in Algebraic Topology

items.title: Cup and cap products with local coefficients
items.statement: For a commutative ring R, the objectwise tensor (L tensor_R K)_x=L_x tensor_R K_x with diagonal transport is a local system. A transport-compatible pairing L tensor_R K->N induces cup and cap products, including relative and compact-support forms, using the published Alexander–Whitney front/back convention.
items.strategy: Functoriality of tensor products proves diagonal transports compose and are isomorphisms. Transport front coefficients to a common vertex, apply the pairing, and retain the back coefficient. The published AW calculation gives Leibniz and cap-boundary identities with fibers tracked.

references.title: Hatcher, Algebraic Topology

items.title: Poincare duality with the orientation local system
items.statement: Assume AC. For a boundaryless Hausdorff second-countable n-manifold M and R-local system L, cap with canonical twisted fundamental classes gives H_c^k(M;L)≅H_{n-k}(M;O_M^R tensor_R L), componentwise. Compact and oriented cases recover the published theorem.
items.strategy: Use the canonical local class in O_M^R. Repeat the published ball/Mayer–Vietoris/exhaustion proof with L: trivialize on balls, compare by transport, and pass to compact supports. AC is inherited exactly from the published exhaustion/local UCT.

references.title: Davis and Kirk, Lecture Notes in Algebraic Topology
references.locator: Chapter 5 §2.2, Theorem 5.7 and stronger form, pp.101–103

references.title: Hatcher, correction to the last two paragraphs of Algebraic Topology p.335
references.locator: Complete one-page correction, including the twisted fundamental class and the two constant/orientation coefficient duality isomorphisms

items.title: Poincare–Lefschetz duality with local coefficients
items.statement: Assume AC. For a compact n-manifold M with its actual boundary A=partial M and an R-local system L, cap with [M,A]^tw gives H^k(M;L)≅H_{n-k}(M,A;O_M^R tensor L) and H^k(M,A;L)≅H_{n-k}(M;O_M^R tensor L).
items.strategy: Repeat the published collar, excision, cap-boundary, and five-lemma ladder with local pair sequences. AC is inherited from boundaryless twisted duality.

references.title: Davis and Kirk, Lecture Notes in Algebraic Topology

items.title: Fiber transport gives the Serre local systems
items.statement: For p:E->B, b↦H_q(F_b;R) and b↦H^q(F_b;R), using fiber transport and inverse-direction cohomology transport, are local systems and are functorial in maps of fibrations.
items.strategy: Fiber transport supplies concatenation and path-homotopy invariance up to fiber homotopy. The published singular-chain prism identity gives chain-homotopic maps for homotopic fiber maps. Applying Hom(-,R) to that identity gives a cochain homotopy, hence identical maps in cohomology; homology invariance follows directly. Transport along a reversed path is a fiber-homotopy inverse, so both induced maps are isomorphisms and satisfy the local-system composition law.

references.title: Davis and Kirk, Lecture Notes in Algebraic Topology

title: Local Coefficients, Twisted Homology, and Duality: Examples

items.title: Circle homology with monodromy
items.statement: For a local system on S^1 with fiber M and monodromy T, the cellular complex is 0->M --(T-id)-->M->0; H_1=ker(T-id), H_0=coker(T-id).
items.strategy: Compute the boundary of a lifted one-cell; inversion of the loop generator gives an isomorphic complex.

references.title: Davis and Kirk, Lecture Notes in Algebraic Topology

items.title: Sign local system on real projective space
items.statement: For the sign Z-system on RP^n, cellular d_k is zero for k even and multiplication by 2 for k odd; H_n(RP^n;Z_sign)=Z exactly when n is even.
items.strategy: Separate n=1 from the higher-dimensional universal-sphere calculation.  For RP^1≅R/Z, use pi_1(S^1)=Z, send the positive generator to -1, and evaluate the directly lifted edge boundary g−1 as ±2.  For n≥2, use published simple connectivity of S^n to identify its antipodal double cover as universal and the published deck-group theorem to identify pi_1(RP^n) with Z/2; then evaluate the group-ring boundary 1+(-1)^kg at g=-1.  Compute the resulting one-generator chain complex.  Finally note that RP^1 is an oriented circle with trivial orientation system, while for n≥2 the antipodal deck transformation has degree (-1)^(n+1); this proves that the sign system is the orientation system exactly for even n.

references.title: Davis and Kirk, Lecture Notes in Algebraic Topology

items.title: Orientation system of the Mobius band
items.statement: The Mobius-band orientation system has monodromy -1 around its core, becomes trivial on its annular orientation cover, and restricts trivially to the boundary loop.
items.strategy: Track an orientation through the rectangle gluing; the boundary traverses the core twice, so its monodromy is (-1)^2.

references.title: Davis and Kirk, Lecture Notes in Algebraic Topology

items.title: Twisted duality for a nonorientable surface
items.statement: For closed connected nonorientable N_g, H_2(N_g;O)=Z and cap gives H^k(N_g;Z)≅H_{2-k}(N_g;O) and H^k(N_g;O)≅H_{2-k}(N_g;Z).
items.strategy: Apply twisted duality with O tensor O≅Z and verify the top group from the polygon cellular complex.

references.title: Davis and Kirk, Lecture Notes in Algebraic Topology

items.title: Constant coefficients miss monodromy
items.statement: On S^1 with fiber Z and monodromy -1, twisted H_1=0 and H_0=Z/2, unlike constant H_1=Z and H_0=Z.
items.strategy: Repeat the lifted one-cell incidence locally, evaluate T-1 at T=-1 and T=1, and compare the resulting kernels and cokernels without depending on a B-page item.

references.title: Hatcher, Algebraic Topology

items.title: An untwisted E2 table misses mapping-torus monodromy
items.statement: For the mapping torus of h:F->F, the formal untwisted table can differ from H_p(S^1;H_q(F;R)_h). For F=S^1 and reflection, the q=1 row over Z changes from Z,Z to Z/2,0.
items.strategy: Identify loop transport with h_* and repeat the lifted base-circle T-1 calculation locally. This compares explicit tables, does not depend on a B-page item, and does not invoke the later Serre spectral sequence.

references.title: Davis and Kirk, Lecture Notes in Algebraic Topology
